correctness.rationale: Rechecked the repaired high-dimensional threshold as well as its finite reduction. With positive orthogonal legs, the active facet and the other coordinate constraints give z_i≤−sum_{j≠i}(a_i/a_j)z_j with z_j≥0. At a longest leg all coefficients are at least one; if any is larger, varying positive z_j and choosing z_i strictly between the two thresholds removes an open set and strictly decreases Gaussian mass. At equal legs the nonright cones are congruent and have angle strictly below the right orthant's 2^(−d). Thus the angle analyzed is the exact class threshold. Changing the singled-out coordinate to s≥0 and putting x_j=sR_j has Jacobian s^(d−1) and a region of coordinate volume 1/(d−1)!, with a slack coordinate completing the d-coordinate Dirichlet law. Tonelli and the gamma integral give the prefactor Γ(d/2)/(2π^(d/2)(d−1)!). Using a common sequence of independent unit exponentials, d times the sum of squares of the first d−1 normalized coordinates tends almost surely to 2 by the first and second sample moment laws. Therefore the bounded expectation factor tends to e^(−1), and Stirling gives the additional 1/sqrt(2) and (e/(2πd))^(d/2). The independent d=2 and d=3 formulas are consistent with full-sphere normalization. The original math was correct; the repair narrows the contribution and credits existing coverage. The finite verifier was inspected, not executed, and is not evidence for the limit.
